- White on top
- Purple on bottom

- White square (left)
- Purple square (right)
- White indicator bar below them (currently under white)
What if the goal is to make the FRAME match the PALETTE? The palette has white on top and purple on bottom. The frame is a single color. So maybe the goal is to make the frame have a gradient or two-tone pattern?
Or what if the goal is to make the BLOCK match the PALETTE? The palette has white on top (50 cells) and purple on bottom (50 cells). The block is 10x10 = 100 cells. So the goal might be to make the top half white and bottom half purple (or vice versa).
But I can only paint using the frame's shape as a stamp. The frame can be diamond (55 cells) or rectangular (65 cells). Neither of these shapes corresponds to a horizontal split of the block.
Wait, let me reconsider. What if the frame can be moved? I tried UP/DOWN but didn't notice any change. Let me check if UP/DOWN moves the frame or the block.
Actually, let me look at the frame's position more carefully. The frame is at rows 24-32, cols 25-38. The block is at rows 34-43, cols 27-36. What if UP/DOWN moves the frame relative to the block?

        if frame_before != n['boundary']:

        break
